mode achieved: static review only; read all 52 in-scope test files (35 design-system, 17 screen 24) and the production files they cover, both overview fixtures, handlers.ts, the real overview route, jest.config.js, window.test.setup.ts; ran 11 grep and python counting probes; ran 0 tests (NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress, proof commands given where a claim needs a run)
verdict: the happy path is covered thoroughly, but every layer of tests (model, block, screen) is a separate hand transcription of the wireframe, written in Vietnamese, with a copied harness; and two field-swap regressions on screen 24 (Delayed tile alert, risk card count) pass the whole suite because Meridian's numbers coincide.

🔴 blocker  Screen 24 tests restate the dictionary copy and the fixture data at every layer instead of deriving them from STRINGS, the fixtures or the model they already rendered
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/*.test.*#restated-copy-and-fixture
- where: the 17 screen 24 test files. The health warning sentence is typed 4 times (model.test.ts:159, Screen.test.native.tsx:191, Screen.links.test.native.tsx:151, HealthCard.test.native.tsx:12-13), although HealthCard.test.native.tsx:16-23 already builds the model that produces it. 'None due from today. 3 milestones and 2 gates are overdue (see Overdue).' is typed 5 times in 4 files (model.test.ts:202, Screen.test.native.tsx:147, Screen.links.test.native.tsx:122, ListCards.test.native.tsx:101 and :124). 'Not built yet' is typed 9 times in 6 files (model.test.ts:42, model.problems.test.ts:18 and :37, HeaderRow.test.native.tsx:125, StateView.test.native.tsx:73 and :177, Screen.test.native.tsx:96, Screen.states.test.native.tsx:116 and :187). The Meridian overdue and risk rows are retyped as tables in ListCards.test.native.tsx:48-85, model.test.ts:219-243 and Screen.test.native.tsx:154-161; the workload rows in WorkloadCard.test.native.tsx:24-29, model.test.ts:188-191 and Screen.test.native.tsx:138-141. The route prefix '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign' is typed in 8 screen test files and the context ids in 9, although handlers.ts:12 and :18-21 define them. Measured with a quoted-literal scan (a lower bound: template literals desync the scanner): in screen tests, 64 of the 68 static strings of strings/en.ts are restated verbatim (194 occurrences in 13 files); 34 fixture strings and ids are restated (93 occurrences in 13 files); 53 multi-word sentences from model.test.ts reappear in other screen test files (106 occurrences). The fixtures are the single source of inputs (every block test calls buildOverview on meridian or showroom), but not of expectations. Variant data is built three different ways: JSON clone plus mutation (model.states.test.ts:12-16), spread-based crowded() (ListCards.test.native.tsx:28-39), and handlers.ts withLongLists/withFreshness (:42-52).
- why: maintenance cost. No regression slips through because of this; the cost is in keeping the copies in step. One copy edit in strings/en.ts:17 breaks 6 test files. Renaming one overdue item breaks 3. With 50 more screens built from this template, every copy or fixture change becomes a multi-file hunt, and agents will "fix" failures by retyping literals instead of reading them. The cause: each layer's tests were transcribed from the wireframe or the plan block, not from the layer below. model.test.ts is already the copy oracle: it checks the literals independently against the wireframe (comment at model.test.ts:5). The other 16 files add cost and no detection power. Design-system tests are fine with self-contained sample text, because input and expectation sit in the same file.
- fix: keep literal copy in exactly one oracle per screen (model.test.ts for en, plus its vi assertions). Everywhere else, read the expectation from what the test already holds. Block tests read it from the model they render: HealthCard.test.native.tsx:87 becomes getByText(healthOf().warning!) and the WARNING constant at :12-13 goes; the ListCards tables come from model.overdue.rows. Screen tests read from buildOverview(meridian, ...) or STRINGS.en. Ids and route prefixes come from one exported fixture constant, MERIDIAN_IDS = { workspaceId: 'creative-studio', projectId: 'meridian-cgi-campaign' }, which handlers.ts:18-21 also uses. Build variants through one builder, overviewWith(base, patch).
- approach-changing: yes, the test layering convention (one oracle layer, derived expectations above it) must be set before plan C copies the template
- trigger: change strings/en.ts:17 'Not built yet' to 'Coming soon', with the product still correct: 6 test files fail (9 assertions) and each needs a hand edit. Rename 'Phase 1 Render Delivery' (meridian.ts:67): model.test.ts:219, Screen.test.native.tsx:154 and ListCards.test.native.tsx:49 fail. Multiplier: at least 287 restated occurrences for this one screen, times the 50 screens of plan C.
- guard-bypass: no lint rule or gate inspects literals in tests: the custom ESLint rules and the boundary rules ignore src/**/*.test.* (eslint.config.js:82 and :174). Coverage and mutation scores do not measure duplication.
- design: yes, a per-screen test helper (`<screen>.test.helper.ts`; the repo already uses this naming in src/design-system/Select.test.helper.ts) exporting the model builder, the fixture ids and the variant builder, plus a written rule: literal copy appears only in model.test.ts

🔴 blocker  Test titles and comments are Vietnamese in every in-scope test file, so a failing test is unreadable for the agency
- key: src/design-system and src/screens/24-project-overview tests#vietnamese-titles-comments
- where: counts by class (python scan with the brief's diacritic class plus the letters a-grave, a-acute, e-grave, e-acute, i-grave, i-acute, o-grave, o-acute, u-grave, u-acute, y-acute, a-tilde, o-tilde, i-tilde, u-tilde). Test titles: 226 of the 227 title strings found, in all 50 files that declare tests (the other 2 files are helpers). Comment lines: 199 of 199, in 41 files. Data lines: 42. Of those, 24 legitimately exercise the vi locale or a language name: model.test.ts:252-257, model.problems.test.ts:64 and :85, Screen.test.native.tsx:260-262, Screen.states.test.native.tsx:89 and :197-199, 'Tieng Viet' and 'Huy' in the three Select tests, and model.states.test.ts:249 'nguyen van an' for initials. The other 18 are Vietnamese sample text with no locale purpose: 'mau chu' on 16 lines of Text.test.native.tsx:150-230, 'Mot muc' at ListRow.test.native.tsx:117, and 'khac' at Screen.links.test.native.tsx:182. Example titles: model.test.ts:21 'OVW-01 first row: title, freshness, work item count, scope buttons, Export not built yet' and Text.test.native.tsx:147 'variant %s: matches the table, no role when there is no heading'. Comments cite ruling ids from the Vietnamese plans: model.test.ts:5 R-B6, CategoryCard.test.native.tsx:23 D-B14, Segmented.test.native.tsx:8 R-B4. The 3-line Stryker fake-timer comment is copied 9 times in 6 files (Screen.test.native.tsx:164-166 and others).
- why: a failure reaches a developer as its test title. The 40 agency developers get a name they cannot read, then a Vietnamese comment explaining the setup. Plan C's agents copy these files as templates, so the share stays at 100% as screens are added.
- fix: translate titles and comments into English, and keep the contract codes in the titles: the trace gate matches them (scripts/check-trace.mjs:3 and :33-57 read test, it and describe titles; contract.yaml requires OVW-01 to OVW-05, BR-24, BR-32, BR-39 and D-19). Replace each ruling-id comment with its reason in one English line. For example, model.test.ts:5 cites R-B6 for 'Sept'; it should say why the expected month differs from the wireframe's 'Sep' (wireframes/screens/24-project-overview.html). Change 'mau chu', 'Mot muc' and 'khac' to English sample text. Keep Vietnamese data only where the vi locale is under test.
- approach-changing: no, one translation pass plus a guard
- trigger: any in-scope test fails (for example the Delayed swap of the next finding, if a test caught it): the reporter prints a Vietnamese title. Multiplier: 227 titles and 199 comment lines today for one screen and the design system, plus about 200 titles per plan C screen.
- guard-bypass: nothing checks the language of titles or comments. The trace gate only requires that a code appears in some title, in any language.
- design: yes, a gate (an ESLint rule or a check in scripts/verify.mjs) that rejects Vietnamese diacritics in src/**/*.{ts,tsx} outside an allowlist (strings/vi.ts, plus lines that exercise the vi locale, marked by a pragma)

🟡 major  Meridian's coinciding numbers hide field-swap regressions: the Delayed tile's alert and value, and the risk card count, can read the wrong field and every test still passes
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/model.states.test.ts#delayed-and-risk-field-swap
- where: production readers: model.ts:68-74 (Delayed tile: value from delayed.value, alert from delayed.value > 0, delta from change = delayed.sinceBaseline) and model.lists.ts:96 (risk count from risks.total). Oracles: model.test.ts:102-118, TileRow.test.native.tsx:108-120, Screen.test.native.tsx:105, model.states.test.ts:169-187 and :209-237, ListCards.test.native.tsx:179-190 and :237-254.
- why: Meridian has delayed.value 2 equal to sinceBaseline 2 (meridian.ts:31-32), and highRisk.value 4 equal to attention.risks.total 4 (meridian.ts:35 and :89). Showroom has 0 for both (showroom.ts:27 and :67) and no measured delay. The fixture and the expectations were both transcribed from the same wireframe (meridian.ts:3-5, model.test.ts:5), so the wireframe's equal numbers make every Meridian oracle agree by construction. The variant tests that do separate the fields assert a different reader. model.states.test.ts:170-173 sets sinceBaseline to -1 (value stays 2) but asserts only delta[0], never value or alert. model.states.test.ts:224 sets risks.total to 6, and ListCards.test.native.tsx:37 sets it to 7, but both assert only the "+ N more" row, never count. A grep of every test reader in src and e2e (tiles[6], tile-delayed, sinceBaseline, .alert, risks.count) finds no other case. Stryker cannot generate these mutants: the mutator files in node_modules/@stryker-mutator/instrumenter/dist/src/mutators/ (arithmetic, array declaration, arrow function, assignment, block statement, boolean literal, conditional, empty expression, equality, logical, method expression, object literal, optional chaining, regex, string literal, unary, update) never replace one member name with another, so the 100% score says nothing here. Same shape, lower stakes: progress.total equals workItems.value in every input (12 and 12 at meridian.ts:21 and :36, 6 and 6 at showroom.ts:20 and :28, 1 and 1 at model.states.test.ts:78 and :80), so model.ts:203-205 could read either field.
- fix: model.states.test.ts:173 becomes expect(fewer.tiles[6]).toMatchObject({ value: '2', alert: true, delta: [{ text: '-1', tone: 'muted' }, { text: ' since baseline v1', tone: 'muted' }] }). Add expect(m.risks.count).toBe('6') after model.states.test.ts:236. Add a check of the risk count chip ('7') to ListCards.test.native.tsx:237-254. Give the singular variant a different denominator (d.metrics.progress.total = 10 with workItems.value 12) and assert the caption's 10. Per screen from now on: one "distinct values" fixture variant (every numeric field a different value), asserted against the full model, so that any field swap changes the output.
- approach-changing: no, three assertions and one fixture variant
- trigger: change model.ts:74 to alert: change > 0 (or value: num(c, change)) and give a project with 2 delayed items that improved since baseline (delayed.value 2, sinceBaseline -1, exactly the state model.states.test.ts:170-172 builds). The Delayed tile then loses its red alert (or shows -1 as the count), and the whole suite stays green. Likewise, change model.lists.ts:96 to num(c, data.metrics.highRisk.value) with attention.risks.total 6: the risk card shows 4. NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress. Proof command: apply the one-line edit, then cd apps/metis && rtk proxy pnpm exec jest src/screens/24-project-overview, and expect 0 failures.
- guard-bypass: the variant tests build the separating input but observe another field. Meridian and Showroom make every other oracle agree by construction. Stryker has no member-swap mutator. In e2e, the Delayed tile is only checked for 'Not baselined' (e2e/web/states.spec.ts:37), and the risk card only for its more row (e2e/web/controls.pages.spec.ts:48).

🟡 major  The three screen integration tests mount a hand copy of the overview route and copy the whole MSW and router harness, so the real route file is never under Jest
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/Screen*.test.native.tsx#copied-route-and-harness
- where: OverviewRoute is copied at Screen.test.native.tsx:37-44, Screen.states.test.native.tsx:33-40 and Screen.links.test.native.tsx:40-47, identical today to src/app/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/overview.tsx:6-13. Also copied: the server lifecycle, the jest.mock of platform/storage, mount (renderRouter plus useRealTimers), hold(), and the OVERVIEW URL (4 copies: these three files and useOverview.test.native.ts:12; handlers.ts:11 and :79 own the path). The nested afterEach(useRealTimers) and its comment appear 9 times in 6 files (also Button, Tile and StateView tests). Measured: 42 non-trivial lines appear verbatim in all three Screen files, and 65 in at least two. The model-building context is written out in 10 files (the 8 block tests, model.test.ts:9-10, model.states.test.ts:9-10).
- why: two costs. Detection: src/app is excluded from coverage (jest.config.js:74-75), and the tests exercise their own copy, so an edit to the real route leaves every Jest test green. Only Playwright can see it: e2e/web/controls.spec.ts:84 presses scope-mine and checks the URL; whether it also checks the selected tab and the scope sent to the API I did not verify (that is part C's scope). Maintenance: any change to the harness (MSW setup, the fake-timer workaround) must be made in 4 files, and each new screen copies about 45 harness lines into every integration test file.
- fix: create one src/screens/24-project-overview/Screen.test.helper.tsx exporting useOverviewServer() (setupServer plus the four lifecycle hooks), mountOverview(url, extraRoutes), hold(answer), OVERVIEW_URL (exported from src/mocks/handlers.ts:11 and :79) and overviewModel(data = meridian, scope = 'project'). In mountOverview, import the real route: import OverviewRoute from '../../app/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/overview'. ESLint allows this, because test files are exempt from the boundary rules (eslint.config.js:82 and :174), and renderRouter accepts the route-map form the tests already use (MockContextConfig, node_modules/expo-router/build/testing-library/mock-config.d.ts:2).
- approach-changing: no, a helper extraction
- trigger: edit src/app/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/overview.tsx:12 to drop scope={scope}, then open /w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview?scope=mine: the screen fetches without scope and shows This project selected, while Screen.links.test.native.tsx:180-199 stays green because it mounts its own OverviewRoute
- guard-bypass: coverage excludes src/app (jest.config.js:74-75), so 100% coverage says nothing about the route, and no Jest test imports the real file
- design: yes, a shared screen test helper and a rule that integration tests mount the real src/app route

🟡 major  Screen block tests re-assert design-system internals by walking the host tree, so one design-system restyle breaks every screen's tests
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/blocks/*.test.native.tsx#ds-internals-in-screen-tests
- where: 119 toHaveStyle assertions in the 17 screen test files (146 in the 35 design-system files). 151 tree-walking lines (.parent, .children, elementsOf(, screen.root) in scope, 89 of them in screen tests (ListCards 14, StatusCard 11, HealthCard 11, TileRow 10, StateView 9, ProgressCard 7, HeaderRow 7, Screen 7, WorkloadCard 6, CategoryCard 4, Screen.links 3). Duplicated pairs: Banner styles in HealthCard.test.native.tsx:88-90 and Banner.test.native.tsx:11-18; Tile label, value and delta styles in TileRow.test.native.tsx:71-72, :99-102 and :126-130 and in Tile.test.native.tsx:76-91 and :153-157; ListRow code color and glyph in ListCards.test.native.tsx:159-165 and :175-176 and in ListRow.test.native.tsx:60-62 and :83-87; the not-built label font and color in HeaderRow.test.native.tsx:120-128 and StateView.test.native.tsx:63-76; Avatar size in WorkloadCard.test.native.tsx:62 and Avatar.test.native.tsx:25-28; glyph character, size and color tables in HeaderRow.test.native.tsx:25-30 and HealthCard.test.native.tsx:26-31, against Glyph.test.native.tsx:8-45. Bar children are reached through elementsOf(elementsOf(elementsOf(row)[1]!)[0]!) at WorkloadCard.test.native.tsx:73 and CategoryCard.test.native.tsx:36.
- why: maintenance, multiplied by every screen, plus coupling to structure. A design-system change that keeps the screen correct (Banner text moves from fsCrumbs to fsSmall, Tile wraps its value in one more View, ListRow adds a container) fails the design-system test, which is right. It also fails every screen test that restated the style or walked the tree, which is the wrong place. A screen test's job is content, links, roles and screen layout; the component's look is already proven once in src/design-system.
- fix: in screen block tests, assert content, href, role and accessible names through queries (getByRole, getByTestId, within). Keep style assertions only for styles the screen itself sets (Screen.styles.ts, blocks/*.styles.ts), and delete the restated design-system styles and glyph tables. Where a block test needs a sub-part, give it a testID in the screen (for example category-0-bar) instead of elementsOf(...)[1]![0]!.
- approach-changing: no, a test-scope rule plus deletions
- trigger: change Banner's text size from fsCrumbs to fsSmall (a design-system decision): Banner.test.native.tsx:18 fails, as it should, and HealthCard.test.native.tsx:88 fails too. In plan C, every screen that shows a Banner fails the same way.
- guard-bypass: nothing distinguishes a design-system assertion from a screen assertion. The coverage and mutation gates reward more assertions, never fewer duplicates.
- design: yes, a written test-scope rule per layer (design system proves the look; screens prove content, links and their own layout)

🟡 major  The stale-reply test in useOverview has no observable that the stale reply arrived; its pass rests on a 400 ms versus 800 ms wall-clock race
- key: src/screens/24-project-overview/useOverview.test.native.ts#stale-reply-race
- where: useOverview.test.native.ts:82-102 (the Meridian handler awaits delay(400) at :87, the test sleeps 800 ms at :99, then asserts Showroom at :101). The guard under test is useOverview.ts:16-25 (the current flag and the key compare).
- why: the assertion is an absence oracle ("Meridian did not overwrite"), and nothing proves Meridian's reply reached the hook's then-callback before it runs. If the event loop stalls past 400 ms (this Mac was measured at load 21 to 25 on 9 Oct, per CLAUDE.md), or a later edit raises the delay to 800 ms or more, the assertion runs first and passes with or without the guard. Whether MSW and the fetch implementation finish reading the body within the same timers phase is [Unverified - confirm before applying]. The test also spends 800 ms of real time in each of the iOS and Android projects.
- fix: spy on getOverview (jest.spyOn on the core/api/client module). Before the final assertion, run await act(async () => { await spy.mock.results[0]!.value }). The hook attached its then-callback to that promise first, so the callback has run when this await resumes [Source: ECMA-262, PerformPromiseThen appends reactions in order and TriggerPromiseReactions runs them in list order]. Then assert Showroom and delete the 800 ms sleep at :98-100.
- approach-changing: no, one test rewritten
- trigger: raise the handler delay at useOverview.test.native.ts:87 to 1000 ms and remove the guard (useOverview.ts:18 if (current), and :25 replaced by answer?.result ?? null). The stale Meridian reply would replace Showroom at about 1 s, yet the assertion at :101 runs at about 800 ms and passes. NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress. Proof command: cd apps/metis && rtk proxy pnpm exec jest src/screens/24-project-overview/useOverview.test.native.ts after the two edits.
- guard-bypass: the only control is the wall-clock margin; nothing observes that the stale reply was delivered

💭 nit  Style oracles compare token values, and 61 tokens share 25 values, so a component that reads the wrong token passes
- key: src/design-system/tokens.ts#shared-token-values
- where: '#6D3BEF' is violet, accent, review, reviewText and series1 (tokens.ts:5, :17, :35, :36, :41); '#FFFFFF' is white, canvas and surface (:7, :8, :10); '#111827' is ink and text (:4, :12); 14 is fsBody, gap and barH (:64, :77, :101). Assertions that cannot tell these apart: Segmented.test.native.tsx:46 and Button.test.native.tsx:12 (tokens.ink), Tile.test.native.tsx:71 (tokens.surface), Text.test.native.tsx:114-118 (text, accent, white, violet), Glyph.test.native.tsx:58-74 (text against ink, accent against violet), WorkloadCard.test.native.tsx:74 (tokens.series1). The token discipline itself passes (probe: grep for #RRGGBB in the 52 in-scope test files, 0 hits; the raw numbers left, such as borderWidth 1, opacity 0.4 and aspectRatio 2, have no token).
- why: the test names the right token, but toHaveStyle compares values. Button primary using tokens.text instead of tokens.ink, or Avatar using tokens.accent instead of tokens.violet, passes today and fails only when the brand later splits the values, far from the change that caused it. Latent: it fails loudly once the values diverge.
- fix: one describe block per style table that mocks './tokens' with a distinct value per key (a generated map) and reruns the table, so a wrong-token reference changes the output
- approach-changing: no, latent only
- design: yes, a distinct-value tokens mock for style tests

💭 nit  Viewport widths and Select options are retyped beside the shared constants
- key: src/window.test.setup.ts#width-constants
- where: DESKTOP is exported at src/window.test.setup.ts:6, yet 1440 is typed on 8 lines (narrow.test.native.tsx:40, :111, :124, :149; tier.test.native.tsx:21; Select.test.ios.tsx:76; Select.test.android.tsx:136; Select.test.web.tsx:45). 390 (PHONE) is typed at Select.test.web.tsx:89, which also re-implements setWidth (:18-26) because window.test.setup.ts registers a native beforeEach (:16-18). The OPTIONS array is typed 3 times (Select.test.android.tsx:7-10, Select.test.ios.tsx:8-11, Select.test.web.tsx:7-10). PHONE, TABLET and DESKTOP are hand-typed as 390, 1000 and 1440 (window.test.setup.ts:4-6), with nothing tying them to bpTablet 768 and bpDesktop 1280 (tokens.ts:138-139).
- why: maintenance only. If the breakpoints move (bpTablet to 1024), TABLET 1000 silently becomes a phone width and tier tests fail in confusing places, and the web Select keeps testing 390 if PHONE changes. The three per-platform Select files are otherwise justified: they test three different implementations (Select.android.tsx, Select.ios.tsx, Select.tsx).
- fix: move PHONE, TABLET and DESKTOP into a side-effect-free src/viewport.test.helper.ts, imported by window.test.setup.ts and by Select.test.web.tsx. Add one assertion in tier.test.ts that PHONE < bpTablet <= TABLET < bpDesktop <= DESKTOP. Replace the 8 literals 1440 with DESKTOP and 390 with PHONE, and move OPTIONS into src/design-system/Select.test.helper.ts.
- approach-changing: no, mechanical
